commit.message:
Ignore manager filters for tree writes on all models

A TreeManager subclass which filters get_queryset() was also used for tree
writes on concrete and MTI models: hidden rows were missed when shifting
tree ids, computing the next tree id, refreshing tree fields, rebuilding or
finding the order_insertion_by position. This crashed or silently
corrupted the tree. Writes now run on an unfiltered TreeManager bound to
the same model; reads keep the filter, since projects rely on it to hide
nodes.

commit.message:
Use an unfiltered tree manager for proxy models (fixes #853)

Since #802, proxy models no longer delegated tree operations, so they ran
through the proxy's own manager. If that manager filters get_queryset()
(e.g. by level), get_root() and other traversals missed rows, and writes
such as making space for a new root only shifted the visible rows,
corrupting the tree. Proxies now delegate to a plain TreeManager bound to
the proxy model: it sees every row but still returns proxy instances.

delegate_manager now also passes _db on, otherwise save(using=...) on
proxies (and MTI models) ran the delegated tree operations on the
default database.

Use Script instead of the deprecated JS attrs dict

django-js-asset deprecates the JS(src, {...}) attributes dict and will
make JS a plain alias of Django's Script in 6.0 (see
feincms/django-js-asset#44). js_asset.Script has existed since 4.0 and
is Django's own Script on Django >= 5.2, so switching to it keeps
Django 4.2 support while avoiding the deprecated form. Require
django-js-asset>=4.0 so an older release without Script can't be
resolved.

commit.message:
Document a concrete recipe for serializing tree writes

The concurrency section only said that client code has to make MPTT
operations mutually exclusive and wrongly listed REPEATABLE READ as the
MySQL default (Django uses READ COMMITTED). Explain why atomic() is not
enough, why the lock must cover the whole table, and show a lock row /
advisory lock plus the model method overrides. Point to it from rebuild().

commit.message:
Reload tree fields of both nodes before move_to() (#257, #568)

move_node() computed the move from the in-memory lft/rght/tree_id/level
of the node and the target. When other nodes had been moved since the
instances were loaded (e.g. moving children in a loop over a pre-loaded
queryset) the raw SQL shifted the wrong ranges and the final save() wrote
the stale values back, corrupting the tree. save() already refreshes
before repositioning (#687) and delete() before closing the gap; do the
same in move_node() for the node (including its parent) and the target.

Also document that transaction.atomic() alone does not make concurrent
tree writes safe under the default isolation levels.

commit.message:
Rebuild the old tree when moving nodes in delay_mptt_updates (fixes #483)

Inside delay_mptt_updates() moves are delegated to insert_node(), which
only marks the destination tree as modified. The tree the node left was
never partially rebuilt when the block exited, so its ancestors kept the
gap in their rght values (rght 6 instead of 4 in the tests, which asserted
the wrong values). Track the old tree_id as modified as well.

commit.message:
Fix lint errors flagged by ruff 0.17

CI installs an unpinned ruff, and ruff 0.17 enables additional default
rules (SIM, PLR, PLE, TRY, FLY, EXE), so `ruff check` started failing on
main and on every PR. Fix the findings without changing behavior: the
ValueError in register() and the Exception in the model_bakery guard keep
their types (noqa) since changing them would break callers catching them.
Bump the pre-commit ruff hook to the same version so local and CI agree.

commit.message:
Fix save(using=...) and delete(using=...) ignoring the specified database (#685)

Tree management operations (insert_node, _move_node, _manage_space,
_create_tree_space, _close_gap) issued raw SQL and querysets against the
default database even when save(using="mydb") or delete(using="mydb") was
called, because TreeManager._get_connection() always asked the router for
a connection (which returned "default" when no instance hint was available)
and the tree manager's _db was never set.

Three-part fix:

1. _get_connection() now uses self._db when it is set, bypassing the
   router. This makes all raw SQL in TreeManager respect a db_manager()
   binding.

2. MPTTModel.save() sets self._state.db = using at the very start so
   that router.db_for_write(model, instance=node) hints route correctly,
   then builds _tm = self._tree_manager.db_manager(self._state.db) and
   uses it for every tree operation in the method body.

3. insert_at() and delete() apply the same db_manager() pattern so that
   tree operations they trigger also hit the right database.

commit.message:
Fix duplicate tree_ids when reordering root nodes with order_insertion_by (#687)

When iterating over a queryset of root nodes and saving each one after
changing its order_insertion_by field, the second and subsequent saves
operate on stale in-memory tree_id values: the first save's SQL has
already reshuffled tree_ids in the database but the other loaded
instances still hold the pre-reshuffle values.

_make_sibling_of_root_node identifies the node to move by matching the
in-memory tree_id in a WHERE clause, so it ends up operating on the
wrong database row. The subsequent super().save() then writes the
(newly assigned) tree_id back for the correct pk, creating a duplicate.

Fix: before executing the repositioning move in the not-same_order
branch, refresh the four MPTT tree fields from the database so the move
always works with current values. The refresh is skipped inside
delay_mptt_updates() where the tracking layer manages its own state.

commit.message:
Speed up get_children() when _cached_children is set (fixes #587)

Previously built pk__in=[n.pk for n in self._cached_children], which

commit.message:
Fix list_editable ValidationError display; update README maintenance note

mptt_results() was yielding plain list objects, so result.form in
mptt_change_list_results.html always resolved to an empty string and
non-field errors from list_editable forms were silently swallowed.
Switch to Django's ResultList(list) subclass, which carries the form
as an attribute, matching how Django's own results() function works.
Fixes #726.

Expand the README maintenance note to explain why MPTT is inherently
hard to keep correct (write amplification, concurrent-write races, tree
corruption from out-of-band writes) and point to CTE-based alternatives
for new projects.

commit.message:
Fix TreeRelatedFieldListFilter KeyError with to_field foreign keys (#693)

field_choices() filtered related objects with pk__in and keyed
levels_dict by model.pk. When the FK uses to_field pointing to a
non-PK field the choices contain the to_field values, not PKs, causing
a KeyError when looking up the indent level.

queryset() had the same assumption: it fetched the selected node with
get(pk=lookup_val), which also breaks for non-PK to_field.

Both now use self.rel_name (already set to the referenced field name
in __init__) so they work whether the FK targets pk or any other field.

commit.message:
Fix get_queryset_descendants/ancestors sibling bleed and get_family delegation

_get_queryset_relatives built a bounding-box Q filter (left > min,
right < max) per group of contiguous siblings. When >= 3 siblings were
contiguous the box was wide enough to capture the intermediate siblings
themselves, so get_queryset_descendants(qs, include_self=False) could
return nodes that were in the input queryset. Fix by also constraining
on level (level > sibling_level for descendants, level < sibling_level
for ancestors). Fixes #517.

get_family() called self._tree_manager.filter() directly, bypassing
the _base_manager delegation that @delegate_manager provides for MTI
models. Use `_base_manager or _tree_manager` as the query entry point,
consistent with how all other traversal methods behave. Fixes #709.

return nodes that were in the input queryset. Fix by also constraining

models. Use `_base_manager or _tree_manager` as the query entry point,
consistent with how all other traversal methods behave. Fixes #709.

commit.message:
Fix proxy model queryset methods returning concrete model instances (#802)

The tree manager for a proxy model had _base_manager set to the
concrete model's tree manager. The delegate_manager decorator then
routed all @delegate_manager methods (get_children, get_descendants,
get_ancestors, _mptt_filter, ...) through that concrete manager,
returning queryset results typed to the concrete class rather than
the proxy class.

Proxy models share the same DB table as their concrete parent, so
delegation to the concrete manager is unnecessary and harmful. Only
MTI (multi-table inheritance) models need the delegation because they
store tree fields on a different table. Add `not model._meta.proxy`
to the condition in contribute_to_class so proxy managers keep
_base_manager=None and use their own (proxy-typed) queryset.

Also update test_proxy_custom_manager which was explicitly asserting
the now-wrong behaviour, and add a regression test.

commit.message:
Fix delete_selected_tree crashing on proxy models (fixes #615)

delay_mptt_updates() intentionally rejects proxy models with
CantDisableUpdates and tells the caller to use the concrete model
instead. Walk up to the concrete model via _tree_manager.tree_model
before calling delay_mptt_updates(). For non-proxy models tree_model
is the model itself, so there is no behaviour change.

commit.message:
Fix three small bugs: is_root_node, _is_saved, DraggableMPTTAdmin N+1

is_root_node() checked only the parent FK column (_id), which is None
for unsaved instances even when a parent object has been assigned.
Now also checks the parent attribute itself so unsaved nodes with a
parent correctly return False. Fixes #617.

_is_saved() checked `pk is None` to detect unsaved instances, which
never triggers for UUID primary keys (auto-generated before save).
Switch to `_state.adding`, which Django maintains correctly regardless
of PK type. Fixes #514.

DraggableMPTTAdmin.tree_actions() called get_absolute_url() on every
row and put the result in a data-url attribute that the drag-and-drop
JavaScript never reads. Remove the call and the attribute. Fixes #782.
